problem: It says a large 'chat model' can become a 'small encoder' for a phone. Chat models are generative/decoder models; an encoder does not chat. Distillation normally preserves the task and architecture family, so this example misleads students.
fix: Distillation is common when a large BERT-style encoder must become a small encoder for a phone, or when a large chat model must become a smaller chat model.

problem: The shared final node 'Deployed small model' has note '4x less memory'. All three routes point to this node, but only INT8 quantization gives 4× memory reduction versus FP32. Distillation and pruning give whatever reduction the chosen student or sparsity level gives.
fix: Remove the '4x less memory' note from the shared node, or qualify it: 'e.g., 4× smaller after INT8'.
